_notes.kind: 'defect' = pass/fail; passes only if every entry in `source` passes. Hard sources (frameDiff, blankFrame, audit:*) decide; `judge` covers what can't be measured. 'fidelity' = the judge compares the shot with each of `references` along `aspect`, returns ranked gaps, and passes only when no high/medium gap remains.
_notes.fields: `shot` names a canvas shot, page shot or `tileSheet`; `shots` sends several labelled images; `segment` names a timeline segment or gameplay script. `crop: true` sends a zoomed crop of the marked/cited region; `crop: "<selector>"` crops a page shot to that element. `marks` draws numbered marks from audit().marks[<name>]. `audit:<field>` passes when the field is true, 0, empty, or { ok: true }.
_notes.references: References show style, materials, lighting and density, not layout. Judges ignore board shape, tile arrangement and elevation differences that come from the game rules, and ignore everything in the config's `outOfScope` (the HUD) when grading other items.
_notes.views: `views` makes an item resolve once per view and pass only if every view passes. `{view}` in a shot name expands per view (ui-{view} -> ui-2d, ui-3d). For gameplay items `segment` names a gameplay script; `at: "after-step"` grades the settled full-page frame after each step. Every item names the views it is judged in; startup fails unless each view has at least one defect and one fidelity item.
_notes.pairViews: `pairViews: true` judges matching 2D and 3D images side by side with shared tile marks and lists per-tile mismatches. The tile spec is the source of truth.
_notes.reportOnly: `reportOnly: true` items are graded and reported for the owner of an out-of-scope area (here the HUD) but never become patcher defects or affect pass counts.

items.text: Board reads as a flat 2D map: no perspective skew, tiles edge-to-edge with no gaps
No frame where geometry vanishes, flickers or goes blank
Props, slab and water rise continuously with the terrain; nothing pops in at once; no cracks between tiles
A slab edge is visible under the board along its whole perimeter
Cliff textures are not stretched
No floating trees, rocks or props
Foam at waterfall crest and base is visible; water flows downhill
The bridge arch is unobstructed in frame and spans the river with water visibly flowing under it
Meeples sit on their features, not floating
Every tile feature meets its edge midpoint
The board is framed so the HUD never covers any tile, in either view (fix with camera framing, not HUD changes)
Every tile shows the same features and objects (cities, houses, roads, rivers, bridges, cloisters, trees, meeples) in the same places in 2D and 3D
After every gameplay step the 2D and 3D views show the same tiles, rotations, features and meeples
The current-tile preview in the sidebar shows the same tile art, at the same rotation, as that tile would show on the 2D board (both come from the shared tile painter)
Each placed tile visibly drops or slides into the correct cell and settles flush with its neighbors; no pop-in, jump, wrong cell or seam
Each placed meeple animates onto its claimed feature and ends seated on it in the player's color
Completing a feature is visibly signalled (highlight or score popup near the feature) and its meeples return to supply
After every step the HUD shows the correct current player, tiles remaining, scores, meeple supply and active view in the toggle
Legal placements are highlighted on the correct cells and readable in this view; after clicking rotate, the highlights reflect the new rotation
No console errors, WebGL warnings, no-op steps or failed step expectations during scripted play
Clicking the 2D/3D toggle morphs the board smoothly both ways and the board stays framed throughout

items.aspect: Overall realism: the board as a whole reads like a photograph of a handcrafted miniature diorama: physically plausible materials, depth and scale cues, natural light falloff, no flat-shaded primitives or untextured surfaces. It should read as a photographed physical miniature, not game art.
items.text: The board looks as realistic as the reference

items.aspect: Board silhouette: the board is a single floating island whose edge drops into its own slab; no extra base plate, ground plane or box extending beyond the tiles. Ignore the background behind it.
items.text: Board silhouette matches the reference's floating island

items.aspect: Cross-section slab: grass lip overhanging the edge, a thick brown soil band, blue-slate rock strata below, irregular eroded edges and texture, tapering underside. It should read as a photographed physical miniature, not game art.
items.text: Slab cross-section matches the reference's layered earth and rock

items.aspect: City: cream limestone curtain walls with crenellations, round towers with conical blue-slate roofs, dense mix of terracotta and slate pitched roofs inside the walls, buildings with visible detail. It should read as a photographed physical miniature, not game art.
items.text: Walled city matches the reference's architecture and density

items.aspect: Ground cover and vegetation: tufted, textured meadow grass with color variation; clustered mixed conifer and broadleaf trees and shrubs at similar density and scale; cobblestone roads with edging; cottages with terracotta roofs. It should read as a photographed physical miniature, not game art.
items.text: Meadow, trees, roads and cottages match the reference's detail and density

items.aspect: Lighting and color: warm low-angle sunlight, soft cast shadows from walls, trees and buildings, ambient occlusion in crevices, gentle atmospheric depth, saturated but natural palette. It should read as a photographed physical miniature, not game art.
items.text: Lighting and palette match the reference

items.aspect: 2D tiles: features read like Carcassonne tiles (city segments, roads, fields, monasteries), painted with the reference diorama's palette and materials
items.text: Tile art matches both references

items.aspect: Environment: the board floats in an open, bright sky with soft volumetric clouds around and below it; no flat void, dark background or ground plane under it. It should read as a photographed physical miniature, not game art.
items.text: Board floats in a cloudy sky like the reference
